newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA'S MANCINI JOINS SENDING-OFF OUTCRY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA'S MANCINI JOINS SENDING-OFF OUTCRY.

text.p: Sampdoria striker Roberto Mancini joined his club's general director in drawing the wrath of Italy's soccer federation on Friday after speaking out against a four-match ban imposed on team mate Sinisa Mihajlovic.
The federation said Mancini had been reported to its disciplinary commission for published remarks which it said could incite the Genoa club's fans to violence.
Sampdoria general director Emiliano Salvarezza was reported to the commission on Thursday for comments "damaging to the reputation of federal bodies" and accusations of bias.

Yugoslav defender Mihajlovic was banned by the serie A sporting judge on Wednesday for a sending-off in a league match on Sunday in which he kicked the ball at the referee, without hitting him. He then also insulted the official.
Mancini, who has had several brushes with authority in his 15 seasons at Sampdoria, was quoted in some newspapers on Friday as saying that the ban was "ridiculous".
"The referee wrote what he wrote (on his report) but people could see on TV what really happened," he said.
"I hope the fans will be calm on Sunday at Marassi (stadium) but we have to be prepared for some reaction."
